candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: interactingDrug
candidates.comment: A drug interaction relation between two drugs, where one affects the action or safety of the other. Also called drug-drug interaction, co-administered drug, reactive drug. Examples: Warfarin has an interactingDrug of 'Aspirin'. Antibiotics have an interactingDrug of 'Oral contraceptives'. Statins have an interactingDrug of 'Grapefruit juice'. Distinct from contraindication, which typically refers to a disease or condition that makes a drug unsuitable.

candidates.label: legislationCommences
candidates.comment: A legislative activation relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it brings into legal effect. Also called brings into force, enacts, activates law, sets into effect. Examples: Legislation A legislationCommences 'Legislation B'. The enabling act legislationCommences 'the new regulations'. This decree legislationCommences 'the policy changes'.

candidates.label: causeOf

Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.comment: The specific date on which an invoice is planned or expected to be paid. Also called payment due date, invoice due date, planned payment date. Examples: `Invoice #123` scheduledPaymentDate `2023-12-31`, `Utility Bill` scheduledPaymentDate `2024-01-15`, `Consulting Invoice` scheduledPaymentDate `2023-11-30`. Distinct from `paymentDueDate`, which is a more general term for when payment is due.

candidates.label: salaryUponCompletion
candidates.comment: The anticipated salary range or distribution for individuals who complete an educational or occupational program. Also called post-program salary, expected earnings, graduation salary. Examples: `Coding Bootcamp` salaryUponCompletion `MonetaryAmountDistribution: $70k-$90k`, `Nursing Program` salaryUponCompletion `MonetaryAmountDistribution: $60k-$80k`, `MBA Program` salaryUponCompletion `MonetaryAmountDistribution: $100k-$150k`.

candidates.label: departureTime
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". Distinct from arrivalTime, which is the expected arrival time.

relations.definition: To continue up to a specified time.
relations.embedding_query_text: until time: To continue up to a specified time.

chosen_property.label: endDate
chosen_property.justification: Forecast continues until a date; 'endDate' fits.

candidates.label: endTime
candidates.comment: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time". Examples: "Reservation 'Dinner' endTime '20:00'", "Action 'Meeting' endTime '17:00'", "Media clip endTime '00:02:30'". Distinct from endDate, which specifies the end date for longer-term items like events or seasons.

candidates.label: accelerationTime
candidates.comment: An acceleration time relation between a vehicle and the quantitative value representing the time it takes to accelerate between specified velocities. Also called 0-60 mph time, speed-up duration, sprint time. Examples: "A sports car's acceleration time is 3.5 seconds (0-60 mph).", "An electric vehicle's acceleration time is 2.8 seconds (0-100 km/h)."

candidates.label: scheduleTimezone
candidates.comment: The specific timezone applicable to the times specified within a schedule. Also called schedule timezone, event timezone, time zone for schedule. Examples: `Meeting Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"America/New_York"`, `Flight Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"Europe/London"`, `Concert Schedule` scheduleTimezone `"Asia/Tokyo"`.

candidates.label: expires
candidates.comment: An expiration relation between a certification or creative work and the date or datetime when its validity, usefulness, or availability ends. Also called: valid until, end date, availability end. Examples: "Software License" expires "2024-12-31", "News Article" expires "2023-10-30T23:59:59", "Professional Certification" expires "2025-06-01".

candidates.label: closes
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for opening hours, indicating the closing time for a place or service on a given day. Also called "closing time", "end of hours", "closes at". Examples: "Store opening hours closes '18:00'", "Service opening hours closes '22:30'". Distinct from opens, which specifies the opening time.

candidates.label: priceValidUntil
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the date after which an offered price is no longer valid or available. Also called offer expiry date, price expiration, valid until date. Examples: An offer has a price valid until '2023-12-31'. The discount price is valid until 'next month'. The special offer's price valid until is '2024-01-15'.

candidates.label: validThrough
candidates.comment: A valid through relation between a demand, financial incentive, job posting, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, or opening hours specification and the date after which it is no longer valid. Also called expiration date, end date, valid until. Examples: "Offer validThrough '2023-12-31'", "JobPosting validThrough '2023-11-30'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validThrough '2024-12-31'". Distinct from validFrom, which specifies the start of validity. Distinct from validUntil, which is similar but for Permit only.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: availableThrough
candidates.comment: A date and time after which an item will no longer be available for pickup. Also called: pickup end time, collection deadline. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableThrough '2023-10-30T17:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableThrough '2023-11-01'". Distinct from availableFrom, which specifies the start of pickup availability.

relations.definition: To be recorded or imaged by a particular device or system.
relations.embedding_query_text: captured by: To be recorded or imaged by a particular device or system.

chosen_property.label: recordedIn
chosen_property.justification: Change is captured by a vehicle; 'recordedIn' fits as recording capture.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: screenshot
candidates.comment: An image or URL depicting a screenshot of a software application. Also called app screenshot, software image, UI capture. Examples: `Mobile App` screenshot `ImageObject of home screen`, `Desktop Software` screenshot `URL to gallery`, `Web Application` screenshot `Image of dashboard`. Distinct from `image`, which is a general image of the item.

candidates.label: recordedAs
candidates.comment: A recording relation between a music composition and an audio recording of that work. Also called recorded version, audio rendition. Examples: "A music composition 'Symphony No. 5' is recorded as 'Berlin Philharmonic recording'.", "A song 'Yesterday' is recorded as 'The Beatles' original recording'.", "A classical piece is recorded as 'a live performance album'.". Distinct from recordingOf, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: image
candidates.comment: An image relation between any thing and a visual representation of it. Also called picture, photo, visual. Examples: "A product has an image of its front view.", "A person has an image as a profile picture.", "This thing has an image URL."

candidates.label: device
candidates.comment: A compatibility relation between a software application and the specific device required to run it. Also called: required device, compatible device, hardware requirement. Examples: "Mobile Game" device "iPhone 15", "VR Application" device "Oculus Quest 2", "Desktop Software" device "Windows PC".

candidates.label: photo
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to a single photograph depicting it. Also called image, picture, visual representation. Examples: A restaurant has a photo of its interior. A park has a photo of its main entrance. A landmark has a photo of its facade. Distinct from photos, which links to multiple photographs.

candidates.label: caption
candidates.comment: A descriptive text or media object providing a caption for an audio, image, or video object. Also called "description", "subtitle", "alt text". Examples: "Image object caption 'Sunset over the mountains'", "Video object caption 'English subtitles'", "Audio object caption 'Transcript of speech'".

candidates.label: photos
candidates.comment: A visual attribute linking a place to multiple photographs depicting it. Also called images, pictures, visual representations, gallery. Examples: A hotel has photos of its rooms and amenities. A museum has photos of its exhibits. A city has photos of its various attractions. Distinct from photo, which links to a single photograph.
